clue.text: One religious system in an undefiled setting indulged in by Holmes

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for the noun: the hobby Holmes took up

indicators.note: a setting surrounds and holds a jewel, so the undefiled word wraps around what goes in it

blocks.note: the indefinite article as a single letter
the Roman numeral for one
a cult is a system of religious worship
undefiled means pure, untainted

explanation.surface: Some religious practice in a pure setting that the great detective enjoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: Sherlock Holmes retired to the Sussex Downs to keep bees, which is the only knowledge the definition needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Apiculture is beekeeping, the pastime Conan Doyle gave his detective in retirement.

clue.text: To put up a record on ice, buy this and skate

definitions.note: a cryptic description of a fish sold alongside skate, not a synonym

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting something up raises it, so the letters are read from the bottom upward

blocks.note: taken as written
LP is a long-playing record
taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions for an ice show: lay down a record, then go skating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skate' looks like the verb for gliding on ice, but here it is the flatfish, sold at the same fishmonger's counter.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaice and skate are both flat sea fish commonly bought together from a fishmonger.

clue.text: About a manipulator in the commodities market

definitions.note: a phrase describing a trader rather than a noun

blocks.note: C is short for circa, about
a handler manipulates or manages things

explanation.surface: Talk of a market rigger working the commodities exchange.
explanation.definitionFit: A chandler is a dealer in goods and supplies, such as candles or ship's stores, so a trader in commodities.

clue.text: Somebody, after a division, shown as supporting tax cuts

definitions.text: Somebody, after a division, shown as supporting tax cuts

blocks.clueFragment: Somebody, after a division, shown as supporting tax cuts
blocks.note: surface reading: a politician who, after a vote in the chamber, is revealed as backing lower taxes
setter's reading: a noblewoman who was shown naked to the townsfolk in a protest to have her husband cut their taxes

explanation.surface: A parliamentary report of a member whose stance on tax becomes clear after a vote.
explanation.walkthrough: A division is a vote in Parliament, which sets the political picture; 'shown' really means exposed, as the legendary rider was, through Coventry.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend says the eleventh-century Coventry noblewoman rode naked through the town so her husband Leofric would lift a heavy tax.

clue.text: Royalty once thus liable to be caught on the hop?

definitions.text: liable to be caught on the hop

blocks.note: first meaning: the epithet of an English king of old

blocks.clueFragment: liable to be caught on the hop
blocks.note: second meaning: not prepared, easily surprised

explanation.surface: A monarch of old who could be caught off guard.
explanation.walkthrough: Ethelred the Unready was king of England around 1000; his nickname originally meant ill-advised. 'Caught on the hop' is British for taken by surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means not prepared, which is both Ethelred's famous nickname and the state of someone easily surprised.

clue.text: Exclamation of a heartless 17

indicators.note: without a heart means the middle letters are cut out of the cross-referenced word

blocks.note: the answer to 17 across

explanation.surface: The cry let out by a cold-hearted intellectual.
explanation.walkthrough: EGGHEAD loses its central three letters GHE, leaving EG + AD.
explanation.definitionFit: Egad is an old mild oath, a softened form of 'by God', used as an interjection of surprise.

clue.text: Evidence in camera? No

blocks.note: first meaning: the developed film that holds the image a camera recorded
second meaning: a refusal or denial

explanation.surface: A question of whether there is any evidence from a private court hearing, answered flatly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In camera' is the legal phrase for a hearing held in private, which makes the surface sound like a courtroom; here it is a literal camera.
explanation.definitionFit: A photographic negative records what the camera saw, and a negative answer is a no.

clue.text: Second loan arranged for accommodation of Zeno & Co

indicators.note: things arranged are put into a new order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A further mortgage taken out to house a philosopher and his circle.
explanation.walkthrough: Zeno of Citium taught in the Stoa Poikile, a painted porch in Athens, which is why his followers were called Stoics.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoa is a covered row of columns, so the meeting place of the Stoic school was a set of pillared walkways.

clue.text: Enjoy the view, my old American friend, from the belvedere

blocks.note: to gaze is to look steadily, taking in a view
bo is dated American slang for pal, as in 'hey, bo'

explanation.surface: An invitation to an old American pal to admire the scenery from a lookout.
explanation.definitionFit: A belvedere is a summerhouse or turret built to command a fine prospect, which is the purpose of a garden pavilion like this.

clue.text: Freebooter to make a double with Red Rum?

indicators.note: to make something is to fashion it from materials, so the letters are formed into a new word

blocks.note: the letter a written twice
taken as written

explanation.surface: A betting tip: back a double that includes the famous racehorse.
explanation.walkthrough: Red Rum won the Grand National three times in the 1970s; a double is a bet on two races, so 'a double' looks like racing jargon.
explanation.definitionFit: A freebooter is a pirate or plunderer, someone who roams about raiding for booty.

clue.text: The Spanish girl goes to party in Manoa

blocks.note: el is the Spanish masculine definite article
a girl's name
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A Spanish girl heads off to a party in a faraway town.
explanation.walkthrough: Manoa was the name given on old maps to the legendary golden city sought by Raleigh and the conquistadors in South America.
explanation.definitionFit: The fabled city of gold in the Guiana highlands was called Manoa, so the two names refer to the same legendary place.

clue.text: Circus performer with an impressive act indeed?

blocks.note: first meaning: a marine animal trained to balance balls in a circus ring
second meaning: stamping a mark into wax, an act that literally impresses

explanation.surface: Praise for a circus star whose turn is truly remarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impressive' is read literally: pressing a stamp into wax makes an impression, and 'deed' hides in 'indeed', since documents are sealed.
explanation.definitionFit: The trained flippered animal is a circus favourite, and closing a document with a stamped wax mark is an act that leaves an impression.

clue.text: Gypsy's taking off

blocks.note: surface reading: a traveller is leaving, setting off on the road
setter's reading: Gypsy Rose Lee, the American burlesque star, is removing her clothes on stage

explanation.walkthrough: Gypsy Rose Lee was a famous American burlesque performer whose act gave the musical Gypsy its name; 'taking off' means undressing, not departing.
explanation.definitionFit: Her act was a burlesque routine of removing clothes slowly to music, so her taking off is exactly that performance.

clue.text: Appointment as Minister to make speech about noise

indicators.note: something placed about another goes round it, so the speech surrounds the noise

blocks.note: an oration is a formal speech
a din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: A newly appointed Minister has to give a speech about noise pollution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister' looks like a government post, but it is a minister of religion.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordination is the ceremony that confers holy orders, making someone a minister of the church.

clue.text: He may achieve settlement too in great turmoil

indicators.note: letters in turmoil are thrown into confusion and come out in a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who brings peace even amid great disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'in' belongs to the letters to be rearranged, not to the signal 'turmoil'.
explanation.definitionFit: A negotiator works out terms between parties, so reaching a settlement or agreement is his job.

clue.text: Improve strength perhaps, by signing him on?

blocks.note: first meaning: a verb, to restore or reinvigorate
second meaning: a noun, the new member a force gains when he enlists

explanation.surface: Building up an army's numbers by enlisting a new man.
explanation.walkthrough: The older verb sense, to restore vigour, is the less familiar one; the second definition is the noun for a new enlistee.
explanation.definitionFit: To recruit once meant to refresh or build back up, and a newly enlisted soldier or member is also called by this word.

clue.text: Boy in bus makes dirge for Derby winner

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so the boy goes inside the bus

blocks.note: a coach is a long-distance bus
a boy's name, short for Ronald

explanation.surface: A lad on the bus composes a lament for a champion racehorse.
explanation.walkthrough: Both definitions are real: the word is a Scottish or Irish funeral lament, and it was also the name of the horse that won the 1926 Derby, a famous English flat race.
explanation.definitionFit: A coronach is a Highland funeral lament, a mournful song, and it also named a classic-winning racehorse of the 1920s.

clue.text: Intellectual's cracked, if one of those in their cups

definitions.text: Intellectual's cracked, if one of those in their cups

blocks.clueFragment: Intellectual's cracked, if one of those in their cups
blocks.note: surface reading: a scholar who has gone mad, or one of a group of drunken thinkers

blocks.clueFragment: one of those in their cups
blocks.note: setter's reading: a boiled egg sits in an egg cup and has its top cracked open, and the word for a highbrow is built on that

explanation.walkthrough: 'In their cups' is an idiom for drunk, but here the cups are egg cups, and 'cracked' is the shell broken at breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang word for a highbrow person pictures a bald, oval head like a boiled egg.

clue.text: Erasmus for instance liable to err? It's possible

indicators.note: possible implies not fixed or settled, so the letters before it may take another order

blocks.note: from the proverb 'to err is human'
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Wondering whether the great Dutch scholar could ever make a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Erasmus of Rotterdam was the leading Renaissance scholar of classical learning, a model of that movement's thinkers.

clue.text: What definition states as significant

blocks.note: the sense of a word, which a dictionary entry sets out
an adjective, as in a knowing, expressive look

explanation.surface: A remark on what a dictionary entry says counts as important.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition spells out a word's sense, and a look that conveys an unspoken message is described with this adjective too.

clue.text: Mother maybe holds back letters for both our houses

indicators.note: to hold something is to have it inside, so the mother word surrounds the rest
sent back means read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: a mother is one example of a parent, hence 'maybe'
letters delivered by the post are mail

explanation.surface: A mother keeps back the post addressed to both households.
explanation.walkthrough: Westminster is called the Mother of Parliaments, which makes 'Mother' look like the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The British legislature comprises two chambers, the Commons and the Lords, so it is both houses together.

clue.text: One involved with arms

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters of the next word are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone whose work concerns weapons, perhaps a soldier or an arms dealer.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition and the wordplay at once: the god of war is concerned with weapons, and his name is a rearrangement of them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman god of war presides over battle and weaponry, so he is the deity concerned with warfare.

clue.text: Deny it's trash

blocks.note: first meaning: a verb, to turn down or decline
second meaning: a noun, rubbish, stressed on the first syllable

explanation.surface: Someone flatly rejecting a claim as rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: One spelling serves as a verb meaning to say no and as a noun meaning household waste, with different stress.

clue.text: A figure sufficiently angular for the Muses

definitions.text: A figure sufficiently angular for the Muses

blocks.clueFragment: A figure sufficiently angular for the Muses
blocks.note: surface reading: a person's shape bony enough to inspire the goddesses of art
setter's reading: a geometric shape with one corner for each of the nine Muses

explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure' suggests a person's body; it is a polygon, and there were nine Muses in Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: The word comes from Greek ennea, nine, and gonia, angle, so it names a polygon with nine corners.

clue.text: Dress, with age, would be 22

indicators.note: if adding age would make the cross-referenced word, then that word minus age is what is wanted

blocks.note: the answer to 22 down, refuse, means rubbish

explanation.surface: Clothing grows into rubbish once it gets old.
explanation.walkthrough: 22 down is REFUSE, whose synonym GARBAGE is GARB + AGE; the clue works backwards from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb is clothing, especially a distinctive outfit worn by a particular group, so it is a synonym for attire.

clue.text: One trick in tune arrangement, to arouse curiosity

indicators.note: an arrangement of a tune is a reworked version, so its letters are reordered
one thing in another sits inside it, so the trick goes inside the reworked tune

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
the letters to be rearranged
to rig is to manipulate by trickery; a rig is a swindle

explanation.surface: A musician slips a clever twist into a tune's arrangement to make listeners curious.
explanation.definitionFit: To intrigue is to fascinate or interest someone, making them eager to know more.

clue.text: Sweet but gullible type

blocks.note: first meaning: a boiled sweet or lollipop to be sucked slowly
second meaning: a person easily fooled

explanation.surface: A description of someone kind-hearted but easily taken in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' reads as an adjective for a nice person; it is the British noun for a piece of confectionery, here a lollipop.
explanation.definitionFit: A lollipop or hard candy is called this, and so is a dupe who falls for any con.

clue.text: Head of state a year from now?

definitions.text: Head of state a year from now?

blocks.clueFragment: Head of state a year from now?
blocks.note: surface reading: whoever will be leading the country after next year's election
setter's reading: the puzzle ran in 1983, so a year on is the year of Orwell's novel and its all-seeing ruler

explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle appeared in 1983, so 'a year from now' means 1984, the title of George Orwell's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: In Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-Four the figurehead of the Party who watches every citizen is the leader of Oceania.
